query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 10 at.% Fe to the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs) will improve its ductility and toughness by increasing the elongation from 5% to 6% and the Charpy impact toughness from 20 J to 26 J, respectively, compared to the as-cast baseline, due to the reduction of lattice distortion and modification of the electronic structure.
generation.conditions: ambient and elevated temperatures up to 500°C
generation.structural_mediator: reduction of lattice distortion through the introduction of Fe atoms that alleviate local lattice strains
generation.mechanism: modification of the electronic structure through the addition of Fe, which donates electrons and reduces the density of states at the Fermi level, thereby enhancing ductility and toughness by promoting more homogeneous deformation and reducing the propensity for brittle fracture
generation.predicted_outcome: increase in ductility from 5% elongation to 6% elongation and increase in toughness from 20 J to 26 J
generation.baseline: as-cast HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs) with 5% elongation and 20 J Charpy impact toughness
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvements in ductility and toughness may vary depending on the specific processing conditions and the resulting microstructure of the alloy.

falsification_experiment.design: tensile testing and Charpy impact testing at ambient and elevated temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the addition of 10 at.% Fe does not result in at least a 12% increase in ductility (to 5.6% elongation) and a 25% increase in toughness (to 25 J), the hypothesis is falsified.
